clue.text: What, unfortunately, not working can make you

definitions.text: What, unfortunately, not working can make you

parts.note: unfortunately or unluckily, as in things going badly
a machine that is not working is switched off

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that losing your job can leave you short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being poor is the plight the whole clue describes, and the two halves spell it out as well.

clue.text: A sailor's said to be a classic war hero

indicators.note: said signals that the words are heard rather than read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a sailor is a jack, so a sailor's sounds like a jack's

explanation.surface: Someone claims a seaman is a hero worthy of the classics.
explanation.walkthrough: JACK is slang for a sailor; 'A JACK'S' spoken together sounds like the Greek hero's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was a Greek warrior hero of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Prefer, when excited, to demonstrate without hesitation

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Prefer, when excited, to demonstrate without hesitation': LIKE is prefer, but no reading of 'to demonstrate' with 'when excited' gives A SHOT; an OCR or transcription fault is likely and no source gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Prefer, when excited, to demonstrate without hesitation

clue.text: Fancy revealing name during talk!

indicators.note: during says the name letter comes in the middle of the speech word

parts.note: to talk at length is to orate

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone revealing a fancy name in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fancy is elaborately decorated, highly embellished.

clue.text: Noted 'address before departing

parts.note: read literally as a celebrated speech given just before dying, a final utterance that became well known

explanation.surface: A famous farewell speech made on the point of leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase usually mocks a confident prediction proved wrong; here it is taken literally as celebrated dying words.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying utterances that became well known are exactly what the idiom names when read straight.

clue.text: Conservative quits

definitions.meaning: a conventional, old-fashioned person is a ...
being quits means owing nothing either way

explanation.definitionFit: Square means both stuffily conventional and even, with no debt outstanding.

clue.text: Unexpected way to get in a couple of parties with soldiers?

parts.note: a side is one party in a dispute, and a do is a party or celebration
a do is a party or celebration
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Gatecrashing two parties alongside some troops by an unusual route.
explanation.walkthrough: OR stands for 'other ranks', soldiers below officer level.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary entrance off the main route is a less obvious means of entry.

clue.text: Aim to follow period of success, given tip

indicators.note: to follow puts the aim word after the success word

parts.note: being on an up is a spell of good fortune
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Ambition chasing a winning streak, with some advice offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' is the verb, meaning to overturn, not advice.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn something or turn it on its end is to tip it over.

clue.text: Maybe left hard, devious and misleading clue

parts.note: Red is a left-wing politician, an example of the left
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
erring means straying from the right path, devious

explanation.surface: A tough, crafty left-winger leaves a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion meant to throw investigators off track is a classic false lead.

clue.text: Nuts and raisins, originally, in cakes mother brought round

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Nuts and raisins, originally, in cakes mother brought round': R in BAKING plus MAD (DAM reversed) fits, but 'cakes' does not give BAKING; likely an OCR misread too far off to correct and no source gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Nuts and raisins, originally, in cakes mother brought round

clue.text: They may follow the odds for various things

definitions.text: They may follow the odds for various things

parts.words: They may follow the odds for various things
parts.note: the phrase 'odds and ...' means assorted bits and pieces, so these come after the odds in it

explanation.surface: A gambler's thought about what follows the betting odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds and ends is the idiom for miscellaneous items, and the answer completes it.

clue.text: Old guard frets endlessly about young offender

indicators.note: about signals the letters are moved around into a new order
endlessly removes the final letter of the word frets

explanation.surface: An elderly warder worries constantly about a juvenile delinquent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the S from FRETS; 'about' rearranges OLD GUARD FRET. The Artful Dodger is the boy pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's teenage pickpocket in Oliver Twist is the archetypal juvenile criminal.

clue.text: He has classified information in his study

definitions.text: He has classified information in his study

parts.words: He has classified information in his study
parts.note: classified suggests secret files, but means sorted into groups: a scientist who classifies organisms

explanation.surface: A spy keeps secret files in his home office.
explanation.definitionFit: A biologist who arranges living things into ranked groups deals in classification.

clue.text: Go to a social occasion

definitions.meaning: have a go means have a try

explanation.surface: An invitation to attend a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Bash means both an attempt and an informal party.

clue.text: Present peer starts calling for attention

indicators.note: starts says the peering word comes at the beginning

parts.note: to peer is to look
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: A lord at a meeting begins summoning notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a demand that someone pay heed, often in protest.

clue.text: Unkind chap, clumsy

parts.note: he refers to a male, a chap
artless can mean crude or clumsy, without skill

explanation.surface: A man described as unkind and awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking compassion or feeling is being cruel, without a heart.

clue.text: Examination set on this writer I don't know

indicators.note: in a down clue, set on puts the examination word on top of the writer word

parts.note: a search is an examination
this writer is the setter, me

explanation.surface: A test given to the setter, who confesses ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial shrug admitting one has no idea.

clue.text: Old English spirit flourishing in battle

indicators.note: flourishing suggests something waved about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ancient English fighting spirit thriving in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: Poitiers (1356) was an English victory over the French in the Hundred Years War.
explanation.definitionFit: Poitiers is a 1356 Hundred Years War engagement won by the Black Prince.

clue.text: Old foreign coin retained in circulation

indicators.note: retained in circulation says the word stays the same when turned round either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An old foreign coin still being used.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a former Indian coin worth one sixteenth of a rupee.

clue.text: Agree to do somwhat short abridgement

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle, to con

indicators.note: abridgement cuts the word short down by losing its end

parts.note: curt means short, brusque

explanation.surface: Consenting to make a brief cut in a text.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion.

clue.text: Really want to get chosen for marathon

parts.note: to long for something is to want it badly
to be drawn out, as from a hat, is to be picked

explanation.surface: Wishing hard to be picked to run a marathon.
explanation.definitionFit: Marathon as an adjective means very lengthy, protracted.

clue.text: Article ruined' both Left and Right

parts.note: left as in departed, gone

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece wrecked by both political wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks political but is the past tense of leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something beyond saving, done for, is a lost cause.

clue.text: Man, for example, ,woman almost upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upwards, reading it backwards

parts.note: Elsie is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man, and a woman nearly upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ELSIE to ELSI and 'upset' turns that to read upward. The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man exemplifies one.

clue.text: Intend to be heard, making an appearance

indicators.note: to be heard signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: to intend is to mean

explanation.surface: Planning to be listened to when showing up.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bearing or outward look is their demeanour.

clue.text: Bad luck in Derby, maybe

definitions.meaning: a British colloquial expression of mock sympathy for misfortune
Derby is an English firm cheese, an example of the type

explanation.walkthrough: Derby here is the English cheese, not the horse race or the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for tough luck, and Derby is a firm-textured English cheese.

clue.text: Novelist forbidding reporter's version

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the news, so this is the word as it sounds

parts.note: forbidding means stern, severe

explanation.surface: A writer's grim take on a journalist's account.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Maybe fools about, getting extremely anxious

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding, an example of desserts

explanation.surface: Idiots fooling around and becoming very nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of fruit puree folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under severe strain or pressure is a state of acute worry.
